skill.name: fixing-metadata
skill.description: Review and fix web page metadata for SEO, link previews, icons, manifests, and structured data.
skill.summary: Improve technical metadata for web pages with focused review rules.
skill.author: ibelick

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around slash-command examples. The system-reconnaissance alerts are metadata review guidance, and I found no prompt injection or malicious intent in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - define metadata in one place per page, avoid competing systems
- keep titles short and readable, avoid stuffing
- manifest must be valid and referenced when used
- set theme-color intentionally to avoid mismatched UI chrome
- JSON-LD must be valid and reflect what is actually rendered

content.value_statement: Incomplete metadata can hurt search indexing, link previews, and browser presentation. This skill gives concrete rules for titles, canonicals, social cards, icons, manifests, and JSON-LD.
actual_capabilities: Reviews page metadata for duplicate title, description, canonical, and robots tags.
Checks title and description quality against concise, plain-text rules.
Validates canonical, robots, Open Graph, Twitter card, and og:url consistency.
Guides favicon, apple-touch-icon, manifest, theme-color, and icon path decisions.
Checks JSON-LD for validity and alignment with visible page content.
Keeps fixes scoped to existing project metadata patterns.
limitations: It does not run external SEO crawlers or preview validators by itself.
It cannot confirm production URLs unless the agent can access them.
It does not replace platform-specific documentation for every framework.
It focuses on metadata and avoids broader search strategy recommendations.

use_cases.title: Pre-Release Page Audit
use_cases.description: Audit a new page before release and fix missing titles, descriptions, canonicals, social cards, and icons.

use_cases.title: Share Preview Cleanup
use_cases.description: Align Open Graph and Twitter card metadata so shared links show clear titles, descriptions, and images.

use_cases.title: Structured Data Review
use_cases.description: Check JSON-LD against visible page content before publishing rich-result metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Review Page Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fixing-metadata on this page file. Report violations, why each matters, and one concrete fix for each issue.

prompt_templates.title: Create Metadata Defaults
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply fixing-metadata to the shared layout metadata. Suggest safe defaults for title, description, canonical behavior, and social cards.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Social Sharing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this route for social sharing quality. Check Open Graph, Twitter card, absolute image URLs, og:url, and canonical alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Design Metadata Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use fixing-metadata to review the metadata architecture. Identify duplicate systems, risky dynamic values, framework fit, and the smallest safe migration path.

output_examples.input: Review a product page for metadata readiness.
output: Missing meta description. Add a concise plain-text summary for search results and link previews.
Canonical and Open Graph URL disagree. Use the same preferred public URL in both places.
Social image path is relative. Use an absolute URL for reliable sharing.

output_examples.input: Check a localized landing page before launch.
output: The html language value is missing. Set it to the page locale.
Hreflang alternates include a page that does not exist. Remove it or publish the matching page.
The localized page canonical points to the default locale. Point it to the localized URL.

output_examples.input: Review structured data for a pricing page.
output: Structured data claims ratings that are not visible on the page. Remove the rating fields.
The organization details are incomplete. Use only verified public business details.
One structured data block is enough for this page. Avoid duplicate declarations.

best_practices: Define metadata in one place per page and remove duplicate sources.
Keep titles readable, descriptions plain, and social cards aligned with canonical URLs.
Verify share previews and indexing rules on a real public URL before release.
anti_patterns: Adding JSON-LD for content that users cannot see on the page.
Using random, request-specific, or unstable values in metadata.
Migrating SEO frameworks while fixing a narrow metadata issue.

faq.question: Does this skill change code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides edits and can produce focused diffs when the agent is allowed to modify files.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it support?
faq.answer: It adapts to existing patterns, including Next.js metadata API, react-helmet, or manual head tags.

faq.question: Can it validate social card images?
faq.answer: It checks requirements and consistency. Live preview validation needs an accessible public URL.

faq.question: Does it create SEO strategy?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on technical metadata correctness for pages, routes, and shared metadata components.

faq.question: Can it review JSON-LD?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks validity and alignment with rendered page content.

faq.question: Is it safe for private projects?
faq.answer: The skill contains guidance only. It does not request secrets, network calls, or broad system access.
